verdict:
PLAIN ANSWER. A homeowner will not be able to tell DeckCraft plants from a photo only in Photo-mode stills, and possibly in a still desktop frame at the Corner and Front cameras. Phones (balanced at most LOD1, constrained LOD2) and orbiting live views will stay recognisably 3D on every asset route, paid ones included. The render sweep estimates the ceilings with good assets as: phone about 6/10 on a still frame and 4-5/10 while orbiting; desktop live about 7-8/10 on a still frame; Photo mode about 8-9/10 on the current WebGL tracer, about 9/10 on the WebGPU tracer, and 9-9.5/10 with server-side Cycles. Reaching that bar needs four things together. Better assets alone will not do it.

(1) RENDER FIXES. These apply to every route, and no asset passes without them:
- opaque canvas (alpha:false);
- honest foliage shading: live translucency that actually renders (today it is injected after outgoingLight), matte leaves (roughness 0.5-0.85, not 0.26), no back-face normal flip, crown/bent normals, baked canopy AO, no pow(0.8) lift or green gain;
- coverage-preserving alpha mips, plus idle 8-16-frame accumulation so no frame shows shimmer;
- PCSS sized to a 0.53 deg sun, and a 0.265 deg Photo-mode sun radius in place of 0.9 deg;
- bed seating and contact shade (P2);
- colour calibrated against ColorChecker photos;
- in Photo mode, real leaf transmission in place of the emissive glow.
(2) SPECIES-TRUE PHOTOGRAPHIC TEXTURE: real leaf, needle, petal and bark texels of the exact cultivar.
(3) SPECIES-TRUE GEOMETRY: true leaf scale, crown envelopes and porosity measured from real specimens, opaque leaf meshes for hosta, daylily and grasses, and LOD2 impostors that keep the silhouette.
(4) Higher LOD0 budgets for showcase stills only, on desktop.

RECOMMENDED MIX:
- Keep the in-repo procedural geometry plan (P3-P8). Change its texture source from SVG masks plus CC0 detail to OWNER-CAPTURED photo atlases: light pad, cross-polarised, ColorChecker. That is the only route that is species- and cultivar-true for all 26, licence-clean for a public repo, and cheap (about C$350-700 of gear).
- Capture evergreens and autumn-state grasses now, before hard frost. Deciduous summer foliage and blooms can only be shot May-Aug 2027; use the plan's CC0 detail until then, with approved browser-AI sheets only as labelled stopgaps.
- Use the PlantCatalog CC BY 4.0 Picea pungens for blue spruce.
- Use free Bentley PlantFactory, through an artist, wherever the bake-off shows the in-repo generator cannot reach the bar. Trees are the most likely case.
- Buy paid assets only if the bake-off shows a visible win and the owner accepts their conditions. Maxtree is the best species fit: about 17 of the 26 at species level, US$26/78/156 per species by Indie/Pro/Enterprise tier, about US$650/1,950/3,900 for 25. No paid licence allows a public repo. Every one needs a non-public origin, extraction protection, Terms of Use and, for Maxtree, Fab, Unity and SpeedTree, written vendor confirmation that a homeowner design tool is not a prohibited editor or modelling tool.
- Fill genuine gaps (ninebark, red-osier dogwood, the two hydrangeas, 'Smaragd', 'Karl Foerster') by commission with a copyright assignment, never by stock purchase.
- Reject runtime Gaussian splats, AI image-to-3D and AI whole-plant billboards.

BEFORE COMMITTING the 34.5-day programme or any spend, run a 6-7-agent-day LOOK BAKE-OFF:
- Species: Smaragd, Annabelle and sugar maple.
- Routes: the plan's procedural build, the same build with owner-captured atlases, Maxtree rebuilt to DeckCraft budgets, and Megascans free scans as a ceiling reference.
- Rendering: identical render fixes, cameras, tiers and Photo mode, judged blind against real photos.
- Paid and Fab assets can be evaluated privately (Maxtree EULA s.2.1(1), Fab EULA s.3(a)), provided they never enter git or a deployed URL.

ranked_routes.route: Renderer foundation (mandatory under every route; not a substitute for assets)
ranked_routes.realism_ceiling: It creates no realism on its own, but it removes the CG tells that defeat every asset: page bleeding through A2C edges, glossy speckle (effective roughness about 0.26), translucency that never renders (foliageLighting.ts injects after outgoingLight), faceted cards, blobby or vanishing alpha mips, shimmer (no temporal AA; SHOWCASE_STILL_SAMPLES=1), penumbras 3.4x too soft in Photo mode, buried plants, bleached colour, and the emissive glow on leaves in shade. Without it, even Megascans-grade assets read as CG.
ranked_routes.coverage: All 26 species, all tiers, live view and Photo mode.
ranked_routes.licence_status: In-house code on three.js (MIT) and three-gpu-pathtracer (MIT). Optional agargaro/octahedral-impostor is MIT. Nothing to license. Public-repo OK.
ranked_routes.cost: $0 cash. Optional ColorChecker: Classic US$74.25 sale / US$99 list (https://calibrite.com/us/product/colorchecker-classic/), Passport Photo 2 US$89.25 sale / US$119 list. GPU cost (estimates): foliage shader v2 +0.1-0.3 ms desktop, +0.3-1 ms phone. PCSS +0.3-1 ms desktop (high and showcase only). Idle accumulation runs only when the camera is still: 0.05-0.1 s desktop, 0.2-0.4 s phone, about 52 MB extra on high tier. KTX2 transcoder about 260 KB gzip, lazy, if KTX2 is adopted.
ranked_routes.time: P0 1.5 d + P1 2 d + P2 4.5 d (already planned). Add about 3-5 d for idle accumulation, coverage mips, the shadow customDepthMaterial, the PCSS sun size, and the Photo-mode transmission patch with sun radius. A WebGPU path-tracer port is a further 3-6 d (optional).
ranked_routes.owner_actions: Approve D1/D2 (make the terms live, physically scaled). Approve the idle-refine behaviour. Give look sign-offs at Corner, Front, Bed close-up, Plant base macro and Tree in lawn, Day and Golden hour. Optionally buy the ColorChecker.
ranked_routes.why: Ranked first because it is the precondition for any route to read as real. The P0 magenta probe already proved the speckle is a canvas leak. Every bake-off variant must sit on top of it, or the comparison measures renderer bugs rather than assets.

ranked_routes.route: Owner-captured species atlases on the in-repo procedural geometry (PLAN.md P3-P8), with crown envelopes measured from real specimens. AI is used only as processing tools: BiRefNet MIT matting, Meshroom photometric-stereo normals, Marigold albedo.
ranked_routes.realism_ceiling: Highest licence-clean ceiling. Every leaf, needle, petal and bark texel is a photograph of the exact cultivar, colour-calibrated. Estimates (render sweep): Photo mode about 8-9/10 at Corner and Front, about 7-8/10 at macro (about 9/10 on the WebGPU tracer). Desktop live still about 7-8/10. Phone still about 6/10. Plant-level realism still depends on the generator's silhouette and branching, especially for canopy trees, so the bake-off tests that.
ranked_routes.coverage: All 26 species, at cultivar level ('Smaragd', 'Annabelle', 'Karl Foerster', the owner's hosta, daylily, ninebark and other cultivars). Seasons: evergreens (pine, spruce, Smaragd, yew, boxwood before bronzing), bark, grasses in autumn state, and autumn leaf variants can be shot NOW, before hard frost. Deciduous summer leaves and blooms: June-Aug 2027 (serviceberry, redbud and lilac bloom late Apr-May 2027). The plan's CC0 detail serves in the meantime.
ranked_routes.licence_status: Project-owned photos (Golden Maple copyright). Public repo and web OK; add an all-rights-reserved or CC0 notice for the asset folder and keep RAW masters off the repo, with EXIF/GPS stripped. Licence-clean tools: darktable GPL-3, Meshroom MPL-2.0, COLMAP BSD, BiRefNet MIT, Depth Anything V2 Small Apache-2.0, RealityScan free under US$1M group revenue (EULA s.6 claims no rights in output, https://www.realityscan.com/eula). Excluded tools: rembg's default bria RMBG-2.0 (needs a commercial agreement), INRIA 3DGS/2DGS/SuGaR (non-commercial), Postshot Free, Metashape trial, Depth Anything V2 Base/Large (CC-BY-NC).
ranked_routes.cost: Gear about C$350-700, each purchase owner-approved: ColorChecker Passport Photo 2 US$89.25-119; A3 LED light pad about C$40-90; linear polariser film about US$15-40 (or salvaged from an old LCD); phone CPL US$15-75; Neewer blue/green backdrop US$69.99; two CRI 95+ LED panels about US$40-100 each; turntable C$20-200. Software $0, or Metashape Standard US$179 optional; RealityScan US$1,250/seat/yr only above US$1M revenue. Plants $0 if captured from stock bought for client jobs.
ranked_routes.time: Owner shooting about 1-1.5 h per species per season visit: about 45-70 h over Oct 2026-Aug 2027. Processing about 1-2 h per species once the scripts exist. Agent build is the plan's about 34.5 d plus about 3-4 d for the capture-processing chain and a check-landscape-objects.ts provenance change (it hard-codes Poly Haven today). Evergreens can ship this winter; deciduous summer looks in summer 2027.
ranked_routes.owner_actions: Approve the gear. Shoot, or delegate to crew. Get nursery permission (Connon Waterdown, Sheridan) and client consent on job sites (outreach is the owner's); RBG needs a paid professional-photography permit. Pick the representative cultivars. Approve installs (darktable, Meshroom, RealityScan via an Epic account, BiRefNet weights). Choose the asset rights notice. Set the default season (summer) and whether autumn variants ship.
ranked_routes.why: The only route that is at once species- and cultivar-true for all 26, licence-clean for a PUBLIC repo and web app, and cheap. It also turns the owner's real advantage (nursery and job-site access) into honest marketing: 'what you see is what we plant'. Its risks are seasonal timing and whether procedural geometry can match an archviz tree, which the bake-off measures directly.

ranked_routes.route: Bentley e-on PlantFactory (freeware since May 2024) used by an artist to author species geometry, textured with the owner-captured atlases. This is a drop-in geometry engine for route 2 where the in-repo generator falls short.
ranked_routes.realism_ceiling: Capable of PlantCatalog-level, VFX-grade realism (examples: https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/8c114e3b958e48298a97cc5da6efb1f0). It has a photo cut-out leaf builder, leaf-cluster and translucency baking, and LOD export. The real limit is the artist's skill and the textures. Likely beats a first-generation in-repo space-colonisation tree at LOD0.
ranked_routes.coverage: Any of the 26, including cultivars, but each is authored from scratch. PlantCatalog's free library has only Picea pungens among the targets. Which species are in the stock content is unverified.
ranked_routes.licence_status: e-on EULA (https://www.bentley.com/globalassets/content/eula-for-e-on-products.pdf): s.1.9 defines User Made Assets; s.2.2 permits sharing or selling user-made assets created in VUE or PlantFactory, provided they are not derived from PlantCatalog assets, materials or textures. Public repo and web are OK for scratch-built models. Keep PlantCatalog metanodes and textures out.
ranked_routes.cost: $0 software. The cost is artist time: about 0.5-2 days per species (estimate). Hiring a PlantFactory artist is a spend needing approval; rates not researched.
ranked_routes.time: Weeks for 26 species. It is a GUI tool, so agents cannot drive it. There is no glTF export: FBX/OBJ/USD goes through Blender 5.2 (installed) to GLB, then meshopt and KTX2.
ranked_routes.owner_actions: Approve downloading and running the Bentley Windows installers and accepting the EULA (https://www.bentley.com/software/e-on-software-free-downloads/). Approve an artist (in-house or hired). Optionally ask Bentley to confirm the position in writing.
ranked_routes.why: A free, licence-clean upgrade path for the hardest geometry (canopy trees, lilac, hydrangea heads) if the bake-off shows the in-repo generator below the bar. Ranked below route 2 because it is discontinued, GUI-only and artist-dependent.

ranked_routes.route: Commissioned work-for-hire species models with copyright assignment, or an explicit public-repo plus web-runtime licence. Candidates: Globe Plants Custom Requests, Maxtree Custom Service, or a freelancer working in PlantFactory or Blender, never SpeedTree or The Grove, whose output terms restrict redistribution.
ranked_routes.realism_ceiling: Archviz grade if the studio is good (Globe and Maxtree are). Realism at LOD1/LOD2 still comes from our own baking unless real-time LODs are specified in the contract.
ranked_routes.coverage: All 26, including 'Smaragd', 'Annabelle', 'Karl Foerster', and Ontario-accurate forms from the owner's reference photos.
ranked_routes.licence_status: Clean ONLY if the contract says so. Default EULAs keep the IP: Globe EULA s.4 bars redistribution and s.5 keeps rights with Globe (https://globeplants.com/pages/end-user-license-agreement-eula); Maxtree EULA s.2.3 and s.3.2 (https://maxtree.org/eula/). Require an assignment, or a perpetual licence naming public git and browser delivery.
ranked_routes.cost: Quote-only, no published rates. Globe: about 5-7 business days for fewer than 5 species, no volume discount.
ranked_routes.time: Weeks, per quote. The deliverable spec is glTF 2.0 with LOD0 15-25k triangles for a tree and 2-8k for a perennial, LOD1 at about 30%, an LOD2 billboard, 1-2k KTX2 atlases and botanical-scale dimensions.
ranked_routes.owner_actions: Approve outreach for quotes (forms and emails are owner actions). Negotiate the IP term. Approve the spend. Supply the reference photos.
ranked_routes.why: The only paid route that can be licence-clean for a public repo. It is best reserved for species where neither the in-repo generator nor PlantFactory passes, or where no stock model exists (ninebark; red-osier dogwood; both hydrangeas at species level).

ranked_routes.route: Maxtree paid library (single-species packs or volumes), rebuilt to DeckCraft budgets and served from a NON-PUBLIC origin in an obfuscated or encrypted container, with site Terms of Use forbidding extraction
ranked_routes.realism_ceiling: High at source: GrowFX archviz models with scanned leaf and bark, 200k-3M polys per variant (Thuja V122: 204,508-726,764). After decimation to web budgets, LOD1 and LOD2 realism comes mostly from our own baking. Maxtree itself says its Low Poly editions are not game-optimised.
ranked_routes.coverage: About 17 at species level: Acer saccharum (V17/26/48/50/142), A. rubrum V65, Pinus strobus V67/V126, Cercis canadensis V2/V55/V144, Picea pungens V63/V157, Thuja occidentalis V122 (species, not 'Smaragd'), Buxus microphylla V10, Spiraea japonica V66 (plus a Low Poly edition), Syringa vulgaris V44, Echinacea purpurea V34/V145, Hosta (several cultivars), Matteuccia V82, Hemerocallis V28/V145, Salvia nemorosa V175, Calamagrostis 'Overdam' V65 (variegated, not 'Karl Foerster'), Schizachyrium V161, Panicum virgatum V49. About 8 at genus level only: Amelanchier lamarckii, Taxus cuspidata and baccata, Cornus (not sericea on page 1), Hydrangea macrophylla only, Rudbeckia laciniata, Monarda didyma, Nepeta nervosa. No ninebark found.
ranked_routes.licence_status: Unclear for DeckCraft; NO for the public repo. Maxtree EULA (https://maxtree.org/eula/): s.2.2(3) allows distribution to end users only in object code, with reasonable measures such as encryption or access control against extraction. s.2.3 bars standalone distribution. s.3.2(3) bars letting third parties use the content in their own projects (level editors and modelling tools are the example), and DeckCraft is a design tool, though it exports only stills, video and PDF. s.3.2(4) bars any export channel. s.2.1(1) permits private use and modification, so a private bake-off is OK. Shipping needs Maxtree's written confirmation.
ranked_routes.cost: Single species, 6 variants, FBX: Indie US$26 / Pro US$78 / Enterprise US$156; Mesh US$36/109/218. Volumes: Vol 122 FBX US$125/375/750; Low Poly Vol 49 FBX US$105/315/630. About 25 species bought singly: about US$650 Indie / US$1,950 Pro / US$3,900 Enterprise. Tiers by total revenue: Indie up to US$100k, Pro up to US$250k, Enterprise above. Superhive Blender editions US$175 per volume. Plus about 0.5-1 artist-day per species to rebuild, and an estimated 2-4 dev-days to build the private-origin container and loader.
ranked_routes.time: Purchase is immediate. Rebuild about 12-25 artist-days for 25 species. Vendor confirmation: unknown.
ranked_routes.owner_actions: Confirm the revenue tier. Approve the account, EULA and spend. Approve outreach to Maxtree quoting s.3.2(3) and s.2.2(3). Approve a non-public asset origin, never in git or git history (54 GLBs sit in public/deckcraft/landscape today), plus Terms of Use. Optionally request a Custom Service quote for the gaps.
ranked_routes.why: The best paid species fit and the fastest route to archviz-grade trees, which makes it the right paid comparator in the bake-off. Ranked below routes 2-4 because the licence is unconfirmed for a design tool, a public repo is impossible, extraction protection in a browser is only 'reasonable', cultivars mismatch ('Overdam', no 'Smaragd', macrophylla for both hydrangeas), and the realism must survive our own decimation.

ranked_routes.route: Free licence-safe models (CC BY 4.0 or CC0) where they exist at species level
ranked_routes.realism_ceiling: High for the official PlantCatalog spruce (an HD export at 40%). Variable for the others. All are heavy and need decimation, LODs and atlasing.
ranked_routes.coverage: Species-level and licence-clean: Picea pungens only, via PlantCatalog CC BY 4.0 'Koster' 12/43 (44,675 faces, 57 MB GLB, https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/8c114e3b958e48298a97cc5da6efb1f0) and 'Glauca Globosa'. Provenance unverified (author must confirm it is not SpeedTree or Grove output): Thuja occidentalis (Gerhald, 64k), Pinus strobus saplings (ASMA3D), Spiraea japonica (maksm, 291k), lilac (LOLIPOP), Acer rubrum 'October Glory' (UESReseach, 1.14M faces, untextured). ffishAsia CC0 Hemerocallis scans and Poly Haven CC0 bark and twigs are texture and bake sources only.
ranked_routes.licence_status: CC BY 4.0: public repo and web OK with attribution and an indication of changes (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). CC0: unrestricted. PlantCatalog free exports under the e-on EULA are NOT public-repo-safe (s.6), so use the CC BY uploads instead.
ranked_routes.time: About 1 day per model to decimate, atlas and build LODs.
ranked_routes.owner_actions: Sketchfab login and downloads, each listed with source and size first. Ask authors about provenance for the unverified items (outreach). Add ATTRIBUTION.md entries.
ranked_routes.why: Covers blue spruce cleanly and cheaply. Too thin to be a programme on its own.

ranked_routes.route: Server-side Photo-mode stills: headless Blender Cycles on a rented GPU, rebuilding the saved design. Only pixels reach the browser, so private or paid assets never ship.
ranked_routes.realism_ceiling: Highest still ceiling: about 9-9.5/10. Translucent BSDF leaves, unlimited instancing, 4K textures and OIDN. With scan-grade assets and calibrated colour it is indistinguishable at Corner and Front. Does nothing for the live view.
ranked_routes.coverage: Whatever is licensed, including paid libraries whose terms allow rendered images. Assets must still stay private.
ranked_routes.licence_status: Blender output is the user's property (https://www.blender.org/about/license/). Pixels-only delivery removes the extraction problem. Each asset licence must still allow commercial rendering, and asset files must stay private. Privacy: homeowner designs and addresses go to a server.
ranked_routes.cost: RunPod RTX 4090 US$0.34/h community, US$0.89/h secure, US$1.10/h serverless; L4 US$0.44-0.59/h (https://www.runpod.io/pricing). About US$0.01-0.06 per still, plus idle and cold-start overhead. Engineering is multi-week: every deck, house, hardscape and light must be mirrored in Blender.
ranked_routes.time: Several weeks. Minutes of latency per still.
ranked_routes.owner_actions: Approve a metered GPU cloud account and a spend cap. Approve privacy wording for sending designs to a server. Approve any asset purchases.
ranked_routes.why: The cleanest way to get paid photoreal assets into homeowner-facing images without licence or extraction risk. It is a phase-2 option for Photo mode only, because two renderers drift apart and it costs real money per still.

ranked_routes.route: SpeedTree (Unity): Modeler subscription plus the Library add-on
ranked_routes.realism_ceiling: High (AAA and film). The best LOD, atlas, billboard and wind pipeline for hitting phone budgets.
ranked_routes.coverage: Library confirmed via legacy listings: Sugar Maple, Red Maple, Eastern White Pine, Colorado Blue Spruce. The other 22 are unverified (catalogue behind login). The Modeler can author any of the 26.
ranked_routes.licence_status: Unclear for the web; NO for a public repo. Unity Professional Artistry Additional Terms (https://unity.com/legal/professional-artistry-additional-terms): s.2.1.3 allows Created Assets only to create and distribute a Licensed Production named in the Order Form; s.2.1.3.1 requires them to be embedded, not a substantial portion; s.2.1.3.2 allows distribution only as embedded. The FAQ says no resale or redistribution of trees.
ranked_routes.cost: Indie US$19/mo (under US$100k); Pro US$899/yr (under US$1M); Library US$999/yr extra; Pro plus Library US$1,898/yr. The trial randomises exported polygons.
ranked_routes.owner_actions: Confirm the revenue band. Approve the subscription and Unity ID. Approve outreach to licensing@speedtree.com about naming DeckCraft as the Licensed Production, browser delivery, the 'substantial portion' clause, and what happens to assets after lapse.
ranked_routes.why: The best tooling, but a recurring cost, named-production licensing and the subscription dependency put it below a free PlantFactory or commission route for a public web app.

ranked_routes.route: Quixel Megascans and Fab Standard listings: REFERENCE ONLY (bake-off ceiling), not shippable
ranked_routes.realism_ceiling: Best-in-class photogrammetry: the bar for 'reads as a photo' at close range.
ranked_routes.coverage: Very thin for Ontario. Boxwood (Buxus), Bigleaf Hydrangea (H. macrophylla; free), Norway Maple (free), Norway Spruce, Lady Fern and others. No hosta, daylily, coneflower, Thuja, pine, redbud, serviceberry, dogwood, ninebark, spirea, catmint, salvia, bergamot or the three grasses.
ranked_routes.licence_status: NO for DeckCraft without a written exception. Fab EULA (https://www.fab.com/eula): s.4(c) requires stopping end users extracting Content; s.5(a) bars standalone distribution, so no public repo; s.6(b)(iii) bars world- or level-editing or modelling tools that allow export; s.2(a) Personal tier only under US$100k digital-content revenue. s.3(a) private use is fine for evaluation.
ranked_routes.cost: Megascans plants about $1.40-7.05 Personal (displayed without currency; matches CAD conversions of US$0.99-4.99), Professional about 10x. Boxwood $7.05 / $70.70. Bigleaf Hydrangea and Norway Maple free. Boxwood raw zip 384 MB.
ranked_routes.time: Immediate download. About 1 day per asset to rebuild to budgets for the bake-off.
ranked_routes.owner_actions: Epic account and Fab EULA acceptance. Approve the boxwood purchase if wanted. Shipping would need written Epic confirmation, which is not recommended.
ranked_routes.why: Use it in the bake-off to show the owner what the best photogrammetry looks like inside DeckCraft's own budgets and renderer. If even this is not 'real enough' on a phone, the bottleneck is the renderer and budget, not the assets.

ranked_routes.realism_ceiling: Good at mid-distance; an older generation and less convincing close up. Each library includes 800x800 alpha billboards, useful for LOD2.
ranked_routes.coverage: Species level: Acer rubrum, Pinus strobus, Picea pungens var. glauca, Thuja occidentalis, Syringa vulgaris. Genus level: boxwood, yew, redbud (C. siliquastrum), dogwood, hydrangea. No perennials or grasses.
ranked_routes.licence_status: Governed by the marketplace. CGTrader s.21A (https://www.cgtrader.com/pages/terms-and-conditions) allows apps where users cannot download the product, with encryption (s.21A.3) and no public repo (s.21A.1, s.21A.6). TurboSquid bans three.js-style open formats without prior approval (s.II.7). No Xfrog EULA found (xfrog.net/license returns 404).
ranked_routes.cost: US$99 per library (US$79 on sale); regional US$199; XFROG WORLD US$599.
ranked_routes.owner_actions: Approve the CGTrader account and purchase. Approve outreach to Xfrog to confirm which licence applies.
ranked_routes.why: A narrow, dated fallback for 5 species. Maxtree dominates it on coverage and look.

ranked_routes.route: Browser-generated AI atlas sheets (Gemini or ChatGPT): interim fill only, with per-batch owner approval
ranked_routes.realism_ceiling: A single leaf or flower can look photographic at 1-2K. Botanical fidelity is weak: in the only expert study (Theidel, JoDLA 11-2026, https://gispoint.de/fileadmin/user_upload/paper_gis_open/DLA_2026/537770002.pdf) botany and geometry scored 2.21/5 and trustworthiness 1.57/5. Lighting is baked in, there is no seed, colour drifts between runs, and alpha is not real (use white and black difference mattes).
ranked_routes.coverage: All 26 can be prompted. Expected to be weak on 'Smaragd' sprays, 'Karl Foerster' plumes, 5-needle pine fascicles, Picea pungens' glaucous cast, yew and boxwood needles and leaves, catmint and salvia spikes, and switchgrass and little bluestem panicles.
ranked_routes.licence_status: The user owns outputs: Google Terms (https://policies.google.com/terms) and OpenAI Terms of Use, 1 Jan 2026. Public repo OK. Probably not copyrightable (USCO Part 2, 2025), so others can reuse them. Google bars presenting AI content as human-made to deceive; label it in the manifest.
ranked_routes.cost: Google AI Pro about US$19.99 or CA$26.99/mo; ChatGPT Plus US$20/mo. One month covers about 150-250 images. Higgsfield gpt_image_2 is metered and excluded unless approved.
ranked_routes.time: About 1-2 h per species to matte, de-light, calibrate and review.
ranked_routes.owner_actions: Approve each generation batch (browser-flow rule). Give botanical sign-off. Approve the provenance label and the rule to replace these with owner photos in 2027.
ranked_routes.why: Useful only to bridge deciduous summer textures until the June-Aug 2027 capture, and only if the bake-off shows it beats CC0 detail. Never the primary source for a landscaping business whose credibility is plant accuracy.

ranked_routes.route: Photo view-set impostors from turntable photos, and Gaussian-splat captures, as REFERENCES and LOD2 sources (not runtime splats)
ranked_routes.realism_ceiling: Literally a photograph from the captured angles. Fails on orbit, from above, and under DeckCraft's sun, because lighting is baked. Splats are the most photographic capture for fine foliage.
ranked_routes.coverage: Potted shrubs, perennials and grasses on a turntable. Trees only partially (wind, unreachable crowns).
ranked_routes.licence_status: Owner-owned captures. Brush and gsplat Apache-2.0, SuperSplat and Spark MIT, octahedral-impostor MIT. Avoid INRIA-based trainers, Postshot Free, and Scaniverse if the Niantic s.6.3 AI-training licence is unacceptable.
ranked_routes.owner_actions: Capture sessions with permission. Approve the Brush install.
ranked_routes.why: Best used offline: for crown-envelope and porosity measurement, photo-match QA at the bake-off cameras, and impostor baking. Not as shipped plants.

ranked_routes.route: Runtime Gaussian-splat plant library (Spark 2.x or three r186 native): REJECT for the yard; at most a later 'see the real plant' viewer

rendering_upgrades: Opaque canvas: alpha:false in the Deck3DViewer Canvas gl props (P0). It removes the verified page-through-leaf speckle on every route. Zero cost.

Idle progressive supersampling in the live view: 8-16 sub-pixel-jittered frames once the camera stops, reusing the jitter and blend code in renderPipeline.tsx:75-84 (dead today because SHOWCASE_STILL_SAMPLES=1). Samples are weighted in tone-mapped space (Karis 1/(1+luma)), and the buffer resets on any invalidate. Cost: 0.05-0.1 s desktop and 0.2-0.4 s phone after the camera stops; about 52 MB on high tier and about 5 MB on a phone. It removes shimmer, A2C quantisation and PCSS/GTAO noise on every tier, including constrained phones with no MSAA.

Bed seating (P2): mulch just below the grass tips, tapering to grade; a soil collar and mulch kept off each stem; contact shade sized to each plant; near-flush steel edging; honest brown, black and cedar mulch. This fixes the 3 in burial and the flat orange slab that betray every route.

LOD0 budget for showcase stills: the plan's 0.84M-triangle estate cap is right for live use. Photoreal stills may want higher caps (render sweep: canopy tree 40-120k, shrub 10-40k, perennial 3-15k, grass 3-8k, about 5-10M for 273 plants), on desktop only, with LOD0 clamped to the frustum or near plants. The bake-off tests whether this buys visible realism. D21's phone showcase cap stays.

Texture policy and KTX2: LOD0 at 16-32 texels per inch of leaf (2048 atlas per leaf family; 4096 or per-leaf sprites only for the macro cameras), LOD1 at 1024, LOD2 at 512 or an impostor sheet. Four families × two maps at 2048 are 179 MB as RGBA8 against about 45 MB compressed, so photoreal LOD0 effectively requires KTX2 (UASTC for albedo/alpha and normal; ETC1S where acceptable). The transcoder is about 260 KB gzip, lazy (basis_transcoder.wasm 245,397 B gzip). PLAN.md D14 currently says no KTX2; revisit it if the bake-off favours higher-resolution atlases. The WebGL path tracer cannot read compressed textures, so keep uncompressed sources for Photo mode.

Optional: port Photo mode to WebGPUPathTracer (same package; 3-6 dev-days). It gives per-instance BVH for InstancedMesh and BatchedMesh (26 unique species meshes instead of 273 baked copies), native-resolution atlas pages instead of 1024 layers, maxTransparentBounces kept separate from maxBounces, an in-browser OIDN denoiser, an FSR upscaler and SunLight. The same diffuse-transmission patch is needed in WGSL. Keep the WebGL tracer as the fallback and for CI (SwiftShader has no WebGPU).

Optional phase 2: server-side Cycles Photo-mode stills on a rented GPU (RunPod RTX 4090 US$0.34-1.10/h, about US$0.01-0.06 per still; multi-week build). Only pixels leave the server, which is the one way to use private or paid plant assets in homeowner images without extraction risk. Needs a metered-spend approval and a privacy decision.

Not recommended now: migrating the live renderer to WebGPURenderer with TRAA, SSGI and screen-space shadows (three r185 TSL nodes). It is about +1 point on desktop live, but means rewriting every onBeforeCompile patch in TSL. Also not recommended: runtime splats, or a pixel-streaming rewrite.
open_questions: Will the owner accept paid plant assets living OUTSIDE the public repo, on a non-public origin with obfuscated or encrypted containers and site Terms of Use forbidding extraction? This is a hard prerequisite for every paid stock route (Maxtree, Fab/Megascans, SpeedTree, Xfrog, CGTrader). If not, only routes 2, 3, 4, 6 and 7 remain.

Fab Personal eligibility is measured on DIGITAL-CONTENT revenue only (s.2(a)). RealityScan is free under US$1M group revenue, and Stable Fast 3D likewise.
